chunks: Al-Hasan narrated to me from his father, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said:

He said: I swear to He toward whom the Throne was ascended, that your father mentioned to me the companions of al-Husayn, neither adding a man nor reducing a man. This nation will transgress against them just as the Children of Israel transgressed on the Sabbath. And he was killed on the Sabbath, on the day of 'Ashura.

key_terms.رُفِعَ إِلَيْهِ الْعَرْشُ: He toward whom the Throne was ascended (a title for God)

ai.seo_question: Who are the fixed companions of Imam Husayn and what is the significance of the day of his martyrdom?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* emphasizes the divine precision in the number of Imam Husayn’s companions, presenting their count as a fixed, authoritative figure to prevent sectarian disputes over the battle's details. It draws a profound theological parallel between the Ummah's transgression against Husayn and the Children of Israel's violation of the Sabbath, highlighting that the martyrdom occurred on a Saturday, thereby linking the event to the archetype of divine punishment for disobedience. This connection underscores the continuity of prophetic history and the specific significance of 'Ashura within the Shia understanding of cosmic justice.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 9. Ḥasan (ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā) narrated to me from his father, from (his grandfather) Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Safwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Ya’qūb ibn Shu’ayb, from Ḥusain ibn Abil ‘Alā, who said:

He said: I swear to He toward whom the Throne was ascended, (Allāh), that your father mentioned the companions of Ḥusain (a.s.) for me without one addition or reduction. This nation will assault the companions of Ḥusain (a.s.) just like the Banī Israel transgressed (the limits) on the Sabbath (the day of Saturday). The Day of ‘Āshūrā when Ḥusain (a.s.) was killed was (also) a Saturday.
